content.title: Boozer twins’ journey from life-saving birth to March Madness
content.text: (NewsNation) — With the NCAA men’s basketball tournament in full swing, Cameron and Cayden Boozer are turning heads on the court for the Duke Blue Devils — but their story off the court runs much deeper. The fraternal twins were born to help save their older brother, Carmani, who was diagnosed with sickle cell disease. Doctors told their parents, former NBA All-Star Carlos Boozer and Cece Boozer, the best chance for a cure would be a stem cell transplant from a closely matched sibling. The family turned to in-vitro fertilization, known as IVF, selecting embryos both free of the disease and a match for Carmani. That process led to Cameron and Cayden. When the twins were born in July 2007, doctors collected stem cells from their umbilical cord blood. Carmani then underwent chemotherapy and a transplant — an intense and risky process that ultimately worked. “Carmani was born with sickle cell, and they found out that he needed to have the surgery, the bone marrow transplant,” Cayden Boozer told ESPN. “The best option was to obviously have us, to have the transplant.” The family has found some humor in the situation. “I mean, they were only born because I was sick, pretty much,” Carmani Boozer joked. “But they saved my life. That’s what their comeback is.” BROOKLYN, NY – MARCH 31: From left to right McDonalds All Americans and twins Cameron Boozer (12) and Cayden Boozer (2) attend the 2025 McDonalds High School All American Jamfest on March 31, 2025, at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. (Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)BROOKLYN, NY – MARCH 31: From left to right McDonalds All Americans and twins Cameron Boozer (12) and Cayden Boozer (2) attend the 2025 McDonalds High School All American Jamfest on March 31, 2025, at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. (Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Duke’s Boozer twins’ life-saving journey Doctors later declared Carmani cured of sickle cell anemia. While the family’s story has gone viral in simplified form, it often leaves out the difficult reality — the embryo screening, the chemotherapy, and the life-or-death decisions the family faced while balancing Carlos Boozer’s NBA career and home life.To fans, Cameron and Cayden are rising basketball stars. To their family, they’ve always been something more: hope.
